When the righteous rejoice you shall be in sorrow, when they are full you shall be hungry, when they are clothed you shall be naked; the day of your visitation drawech nigh, and the hour of your destruction is not slumbering; "death and hell is moved from beneath to receive you at your coming," and everlasting shame shall cover you forever and ever.

SIDNEY RIGDON

Pillsburgh, May 18, 1845.

Elijah R. Swackhammer. To the Editor of the Messenger and Advocate of the Kingdom and Church of Christ.

Beloved Brother:- This morning we left Beaver county, in order to porclaim the Kingdom, and the gospel of the Kingdom to the people of other towns and villages, that they also, may have an opportunity of having the gospel of their salvation and be saved by an obedience to it. Brother J. Hatch Jr and Brother Ellis also left, for the same purpose, and have gone to Washington, and other counties.

Our meetings were generally well attended, and the people were divided in there opinions as it respects the work-some contending for and some against it. We anticipate some being brought out of darkness into the light of God, in that section.

Přemit me sir; to relate a curious circumstance. We held two meetings in a certain village, and the house was well filled. The Kingdom and its gospel were the subjects of discurse the people seemed to be well satisfied-accordingly we left another appointment, and went to fulfill it-there were three or four persons present we left another appointment and went to fulfill it-not one person but those of the family. By this time we felt very anxious to know the cause, accordingly inquired particularly, and, was candidly inforined, by the people of the house that the people, with whom they had convers. ed said they had no faut to find with us, nor our doctrine but we were Mormons, therefore would not countenance us or come to hear us.

This notion of our being members of tha corrupt body of people originated in the faces of their having preached, in that section o the country, some things pertaining to the Kingdom and Chure of Chris; witch has been organized since they ceased to be ministers of righteousness; and all the truth, co mal-er by whom it is held, will be lodged in this kingdom, and church; and the name of any people, that holds some truth, may be applied to us with as much propriety as that of the Mormons. And if we are to be distingushed by former names we must be called the Mormon, Methodist, Presbyterian, Baptist, &c. &c. Church, for the members of the kingdom aud Church of Christ organized the 7th and 8th days of April 1845, in Pittsburgh Pa, are from a nong this, and almost every other class of people; and if those with whom we are not be inconnected in a church capacity, will admit that faith in Jesus of Nazarath, as the Son of God, and repentance toward God, and baptism in the name of Christ, by some one having authority from him, and the laying on of the hands such and prayer for the reception of the Holy Ghost, and the receiving of it, consti-tutes a body of people the Church of Christ, with officers in it according to the will of God, then we are entiteld to the name by which we are called, and which we wish to be known, by all people. And whether the people will, or will not, admit that the fors going is God's order of constituing hischurch and kingdom we know that it is, and that they do us great injustice in calling us by any other name. Therefore we hope that the brethren, they and all people, will call us by the right name. And be it known unto all, that every one whether mentbers of the Mormon or any other church, or of ho church, enter the kingdom and church of Christ, enter it by baptism. For Christ gave himself for the church that he might sanctify and cleans it with the washing of water in obedience to the word. And the apostolia Ephesian Church, after they had been baptised twice. were commanded to re-pent and be baptised againzor to do their first works, in the which baptism, of course, was included. See Acts the last of the 18th and first of the 19th, and Revelations 2nd.
